1.title: Snip off one clear plug
1.say: Cut one clear plug off the cable. Leave the other plug on the cable.
placements: clear plug on one end of network cable → cut off close behind plug leaving flat bare cut end with other plug staying on opposite end (in the video: blue cable on dark table)
cutting blades of cutters → around outer covering just behind clear plug to snip it off (in the video: yellow and black handled tool on dark wood table)
watch_for: if both ends have no plug you cut both ends, cut only one end
if inner wires are cut uneven the cut was too far back, cut close behind the plug
1.check_yourself: It should look like one plug left and one flat bare end.
1.safety: Keep fingers away from the cutter blades while you squeeze.

2.title: Strip the outer covering back
2.say: Hold the stripping tool about one inch from the cut tip. Squeeze the stripping tool lightly. Pull the loose outer covering off.
placements: outer covering at cut end → stripped back about one inch to expose eight small inner wires (in the video: blue covering on dark wood table)
jaws of stripping tool → around outer covering about one inch from cut tip squeezed lightly to cut only outer covering (in the video: yellow handled stripper)
watch_for: if tiny inner wires are cut or nicked you squeezed too hard, squeeze only the outer covering
if less than fingertip of wire shows you stripped too little, strip about one inch
2.check_yourself: It should look like eight tiny wires sticking from outer covering.
2.safety: Keep fingers clear of the stripping tool blades while squeezing.

3.title: Untwist and straighten tiny wires
3.say: Untwist every pair with your fingertips. Rub each wire straight, so it lies flat. Snip the white string short at the covering.
placements: eight inner wires at cut end → separated from twisted pairs into eight single straight wires fanned out from outer covering (in the video: wires fanned on dark wood table)
white string filler inside cable → snipped short at edge of outer covering and removed (in the video: small white thread next to wires)
watch_for: if wires spring back curly they are still twisted, keep rubbing until straight
if white string sticks out past wires it will block the plug, snip it short at the covering
3.check_yourself: It should look like eight separate straight wires fanned apart.

4.title: Slide on the rubber cover
4.say: Slide the rubber cover onto the cut end. Push it far down, so it stays out of the way.
placements: small rubber cover → slid narrow end first over cut end and down outer covering below exposed wires with wide opening facing wires (in the video: small blue boot around blue cable below wires)
watch_for: if the cover bunches at the wires the wide opening faces the wrong way, turn it around
if the cover sits up among the wires it will block the next step, push it far down the cable
4.check_yourself: It should look like a loose cover sitting far below bare wires.

5.title: Line up wires green first
5.say: Arrange the eight wires flat in green first order. Pinch them flat, so none crosses over another. Snip the tips straight and even.
placements: white and green striped wire → position 1 leftmost with plug clip facing away and down (in the video: leftmost wire matching 568A diagram top left on screen)
green wire → position 2 second from left with clip facing away (in the video: second wire in 568A diagram)
white and orange striped wire → position 3 third from left with clip facing away (in the video: third wire in 568A diagram)
blue wire → position 4 fourth from left with clip facing away (in the video: fourth wire in 568A diagram)
white and blue striped wire → position 5 fifth from left with clip facing away (in the video: fifth wire in 568A diagram)
orange wire → position 6 sixth from left with clip facing away (in the video: sixth wire in 568A diagram)
white and brown striped wire → position 7 seventh from left with clip facing away (in the video: seventh wire in 568A diagram)
brown wire → position 8 rightmost with clip facing away (in the video: eighth wire in 568A diagram)
tips of eight lined up wires → trimmed straight and even with cutters to same length to fit plug (in the video: even flat tips held over finger)
watch_for: if green wires are not first two on the left the order is wrong, start again with white and green leftmost
if tips are jagged or uneven some wires will miss, snip again straight across
5.check_yourself: It should look like eight flat parallel wires green first and even tips.
5.safety: Keep fingertips away from the cutter edge while snipping.

6.title: Push wires into clear plug
6.say: Hold the clear plug with the clip facing down. Push the eight wires far, so tips touch the front.
placements: ordered eight wires → pushed fully into back of new clear plug with clip facing down and white and green wire leftmost until tips touch front metal teeth and outer covering just enters plug (in the video: wires reaching front of clear plug held over dark table)
watch_for: if wire colors swap inside the plug the order flipped while pushing, pull out and line up again
if wire tips stop short of the front metal teeth you did not push far, push until they touch the front
6.check_yourself: It should look like colored wires reaching the front inside clear plug.

7.title: Squeeze the plug tight
7.say: Set the plug into the squeezing tool. Check the outer covering sits inside the plug. Squeeze hard, so the teeth bite the wires.
placements: clear plug with wires → set into crimp slot of squeezing tool with clip side out (in the video: plug in black tool with orange handles on dark table)
handles of squeezing tool → squeezed firmly shut to press metal teeth down into wires and grip outer covering inside plug (in the video: tool closed around plug)
watch_for: if the plug pulls off easily you did not squeeze hard enough, squeeze again firmly
if the outer covering hangs outside the plug the connection will break, push covering inside before squeezing
7.check_yourself: It should look like a tight plug with teeth pressed and covering inside.
7.safety: Keep fingers out of the squeezing jaws while you squeeze.

8.title: Slide cover over plug
8.say: Slide the rubber cover up over the plug back. Push until it sits snug around the plug.
placements: small rubber cover → slid up outer covering and over back of crimped clear plug until snug around plug (in the video: blue boot covering back of clear plug on blue cable)
watch_for: if the cover stops before the plug the cable is kinked, straighten and push again
if the plug back stays exposed the cover is not up far, push until it hugs the plug
8.check_yourself: It should look like the cover hugging the back of the plug.
